column1: # The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on.

# nninitStartup asks SetHeapSize 0x18ce00000 (6.2 GB) with the 9 GB pool, as Mario Kart World. 256 MB in front + 4 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 8 GB heap region: a starting split, to be measured
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
# The picture: docked the game draws 2048x1152 with 3D views of 1536x864 at graphics scale tier 1, the tier the host answers docked, and 2560x1440 with 1920x1080 at tier 0 (about 56 % more

# pixels: 17.2 against 13.9 ms of GPU a frame over Kakariko Village on an M3 Pro, 57 fps where tier 1 holds 60). The 60 fps here was tuned at tier 1; the Mac settings window's Full resolution answers tier 0

# The render scale stub (patches.py render_scale) stores the host's factor as the scene's scale, a fraction of the picture, of which the game's own 3D views are 0.75 docked (1536 of 2048, 1920 of 2560)
# and handheld (1440 of 1920): 0.8 there drew more than the game does. The loader multiplies the setting by this, so 100 % is the game's own size and anything below is smaller
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here
# Texture filtering: the game asks for 1x and 2x anisotropy only, so ground and walls blur where the camera looks along them. 16x on its mipmapped linear samplers cost nothing measurable on an
# M3 Pro (GPU p50 12.0 ms either way at Hyrule Castle; 13.4 against 13.9-14.5 ms at a heavier save, one run each); the Mac settings window's Texture filtering changes it
# The game's upscaling step (agl_ndsr_vr's network, which takes the frames before into account) is drawn by MetalFX's spatial scaler on a Mac: the network took about 1.6 ms of GPU a frame more on an
# M3 Pro and showed a double image of the player character while turning. The 60 fps here was tuned with MetalFX; the Mac settings window's Game's upscaler gives the network back

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
# The game submits a frame's commands behind an event its CPU signals once the frame before has left the GPU, so the GPU starts each frame with nothing queued and waits for the
# replay: with Metal encoding on its own thread a GPU-bound Hyrule Field scene went 55.3-55.8 -> 56.5-56.9 fps (Apple M4 Pro, three runs a side, interleaved)
# (this branch) left off: the event gate (DM_NVN_EVENT_GATE, nvn_queue.inc) replays those commands ahead instead, and it does not run with the encode thread
